{{short description|German mathematician}}
{{use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=July 2020}}
'''Christiane Tammer''' (née Gerstewitz, also published as Christiane Gerth){{sfnp|Weidner|2017}} is a German mathematician known for her work on [[mathematical optimization]]. She is a professor in the Institute of Mathematics of [[Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg]],{{r|halle}} and editor-in-chief of ''Optimization: A Journal of Mathematical Programming and Operations Research''.{{r|opt}}

Tammer is the namesake of the Gerstewitz functions or Gerstewitz [[Functional (mathematics)|functionals]] in [[vector optimization]] and its generalizations.{{r|gerstewitz}}

==Education==
Tammer earned a doctorate ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) in 1984 at the [[Technical University Leuna-Merseburg]]. Her dissertation, ''Beiträge zur Dualitätstheorie der nichtlinearen Vektoroptimierung'', was supervised by {{ill|Alfred Göpfert|de}}.{{r|mg}} She earned a [[habilitation]] at Halle in 1991.{{r|hab}}

==Books==
Tammer is the author of books including:
*''Variational Methods in Partially Ordered Spaces'' (with Alfred Göpfert, Hassan Riahi, and Constantin Zălinescu, Springer, 2003){{r|vm}}
*''Set-valued Optimization: An Introduction with Applications'' (with Akhtar A. Khan and Constantin Zălinescu, Springer, 2014){{r|svo}}
*''Scalarization and Separation by Translation Invariant Functions'' (with Petra Weidner, Springer, 2020)

She is the co-editor, with Frank Heyde, of ''Festschrift in celebration of Prof. Dr. Wilfried Grecksch's 60th birthday'' (Shaker, 2008).
